title: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data
abstract: arXiv:2611.16933v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Full-duplex spoken dialogue models learn turn-taking, overlaps and backchannels from conversations recorded with one channel per speaker, but most available conversational audio is a single mono mix. We present Kezek, a model that turns a mono recording of exactly two people into one track per person with the original length and timing; overlaps and short replies ("yeah", "mm-hm") stay on the track of the person who said them. Kezek decides who speaks when and who is who once for the whole recording (stage 1: a two-voice activity model guided by a speaker fingerprint trained to be insensitive to phase), and a conditioned time-domain separator only carries out that decision (stage 2), with outputs that always sum to the input. Standard separation metrics miss the failures that matter for dialogue data, so we report short-reply retention, leakage onto the other person's solo, channel swaps and coverage. Against the open pipeline pyannote

translated_title: Kezek：将单声道双人对话拆分为按说话人划分的音轨以构建全双工对话数据
translated_abstract: 全双工语音对话模型需要从每个说话人单独录音的对话中学习话轮转换、语音重叠和反馈语，但大多数可用的对话音频都是单一的单声道混合录音。我们提出了Kezek，一个能将恰好两个人的单声道录音转换为每人一条音轨的模型，并保持原始长度和时间对齐；重叠部分和简短回应（如"yeah"、"mm-hm"）会保留在实际说话者的音轨上。Kezek对整段录音一次性决定“谁在何时说话”和“谁是谁”（第一阶段：由经过训练、对相位不敏感的说话人指纹引导的双人语音活动模型），而条件化的时域分离器仅执行该决定（第二阶段），其输出始终可以相加还原为输入。标准的分离指标无法捕捉对对话数据至关重要的失败模式，因此我们报告了简短回应保留率、泄漏到他人音轨的情况、声道互换以及覆盖率。与开源流水线pyannote相比……
tldr: 提出Kezek模型，可将双人单声道对话录音自动分离为每人一条的独立音轨，同时保留时间对齐和简短回应的归属，从而为全双工语音对话模型生成可用的训练数据。
en_tdlr: Kezek splits a mono two-person conversation recording into per-speaker tracks while preserving timing and short-reply attribution, enabling usable training data for full-duplex spoken dialogue models.
